evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: 6.1 Process steps – required actions by activity

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: 1. Check carton for damage and ESD labels. 2. Outside the EPA, keep cartons sealed; they may be moved on ordinary carts. 3. Carry to the EPA receiving bench. 4. Grounded, open the carton and inspect the shielding bag/container; open the bag only if a count or inspection is required, and then only at the bench. 5. Log lot/date code, quantity and any humidity-card reading.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: 1. Wrist strap tested and worn. 2. Pick from the ESD location; open bags only on a grounded work surface. 3. Reseal remainder in a shielding bag; reseal MSD bags per J-STD-033 and replace desiccant/indicator card as required. 4. Pack the issue quantity in a closed shielding bag or conductive tote, label, and close.

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: 5. Environment and Storage Conditions

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: Store ESDS only in designated, labelled ESD racks/cabinets/bins. Keep non-ESD materials (cardboard overflow, plastic wrap, personal items) out of these locations. Remove insulators from within about 30 cm (12 in) of exposed ESDS; where this cannot be done, use an ionizer (see 7.1).

evidence.source_quote: handling and storage of ESD-sensitive items
evidence.output_quote: 1. Place items in their original or equal ESD container. 2. Close bags (fold, no staples or tape). 3. Put in assigned labelled ESD location; no stacking beyond rack rating, no loose items. 4. Update location in the inventory system; apply FIFO/FEFO.

task_fulfillment.rationale: The deliverable is a well-structured, comprehensive Word SOP covering ESD handling, storage, grounding, packaging hierarchy, verification schedules, quarantine, and training requirements, referencing IPC-A-610G and related ESD standards. It appropriately flags site-specific parameters for confirmation without introducing unnecessary holds. Minor omissions exist regarding specific mention of ESD-approved gloves (R40) and conductive foam inserts/trays (R43), which are captured in the requirement checks.
